title: Bergbahnen Oberperfuss Rangger Köpfl
name: Bergbahnen Oberperfuss Rangger Köpfl
kurzbeschreibung: The Bergbahnen Oberperfuss to the Rangger Köpfl: 8-seater gondola, Geisterwanderweg for families, panoramic lake, and sweeping views of the Inntal.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Bergbahnen Oberperfuss Rangger Köpfl provide access to the sun-drenched home mountain of Oberperfuss on an elevated plateau roughly 15 kilometres west of Innsbruck. Operating in two sections, the modern Peter Anich 8-seater gondola lift transports visitors and hikers comfortably from 820 metres above sea level via Stiglreith (1,363 m) up to Sulzstich at around 1,560 metres. Set against the majestic backdrop of the Stubaier Alpen and the Wettersteingebirge, the Rangger Köpfl delights as an exceptionally family-friendly adventure and scenic mountain boasting gentle alpine meadows, rustic huts, and sweeping vistas over the central Inntal.

Ghost Trail & Nature Enjoyment

In recent years, the Rangger Köpfl has blossomed into one of the most popular local recreation destinations in the greater Innsbruck area. An undisputed highlight for families with children is the Geisterwanderweg Oberperfuss: along a stroller-friendly forest road connecting Stiglreith and Sulzstich, 21 talking, artfully carved tree spirits share thrilling legends and alpine secrets. At the push of a button, the wooden forest guardians spring to life and captivate young hikers. At the terminus of the second gondola section lies the picturesque Speichersee Sulzstich reservoir lake, where shoreline relaxation loungers and a barefoot trail invite visitors to unwind. Ambitious peak-baggers can continue their hike from here via the Rosskogelhütte up to the 1,939-metre summit of the Rangger Köpfl or the striking summit cross of the Rosskogel (2,646 m).

Visit & Getting There

During the summer season from mid-June to late October, the cable car is open from Tuesday to Sunday from 09:00 to 16:30 (operating daily during Tyrolean summer school holidays). Summer lift fares (season 2025/2026): round trip to Sulzstich adults approx. €22.00, youth approx. €17.50, children (born 2010–2018) approx. €13.00; children under 6 ride free. With the regional Welcome Card for overnight guests, trips are discounted or free of charge. Public transport: from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, VVT bus line 4165 runs every 30 minutes directly to the valley station (stop Oberperfuss Bergbahnen). By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Zirl Ost or Kematen, continuing to Oberperfuss; large free parking lots are available right at the valley station.

Tips

Thanks to continuous 8-seater gondola service and wide forest tracks, the entire area between the valley station, Stiglreith, and the ghost trail up to Sulzstich is exemplarily barrier-free and perfectly tailored to strollers and wheelchair users. Pay a visit to the popular Panoramarestaurant Stiglreith or the rustic Almgasthaus Sulzstich to taste homemade variations of Tyrolean dumplings.
